title: Investigating the Three-dimensional Flow Separation Induced by a Model Vocal Fold Polyp
protocol: Position a wall-mounted prolate hemispheroid on the test section floor of a suction type wind tunnel with a 5:1 contraction ratio.
Use oil-flow visualization to investigate unsteady, three-dimensional flow separation around the model vocal fold polyp.
Acquire wall pressure measurements using a sixteen channel scanning pressure transducer equipped with piezoresistive pressure sensors.
Install static pressure taps upstream and downstream of the model vocal fold polyp for surface pressure measurements.
Connect the static pressure taps flush-mounted upstream and downstream to the scanning pressure device via stainless steel tubulations.
Ensure oil-flow visualization is not conducted simultaneously with wall pressure measurements to prevent fouling.
Generate a three-dimensional CAD model of a prolate hemispheroid measuring 5.08 cm long, 2.54 cm wide, and 1.27 cm tall.
Mount a 2.54 cm square base that is 0.64 cm thick to the bottom of the model vocal fold polyp for anchoring purposes.
Export the CAD model as an STL file with a resolution of at least 600 dots/in to ensure surface smoothness.
Upload the STL file into the printing software and print the model using a high-resolution three-dimensional printer with a build layer resolution of at least 20 μm.
Mill a 2.54 cm square hole approximately 0.85 cm deep into the wind tunnel test section floor removable plate to mount the model vocal fold polyp for testing.
Position the hole in the center of the test section width and at the desired downstream location for testing.
Cover the test section surface inside of the wind tunnel with white adhesive paper.
Smooth the adhesive paper to ensure no bumps or creases.
Cut a hole in the adhesive paper above the square hole for the model polyp anchor.
Insert the protuberance (model vocal fold polyp) into the anchor position.
Mount a high resolution camera above the wind tunnel test section.
Focus the camera on the chosen field of view including the model polyp and surrounding area.
Set the camera acquisition parameters for testing.
Prepare the flow-visualization oil mixture by combining baby oil, copy toner powder, and kerosene in a 7:1:2 ratio.
Mix 35 ml baby oil with 5 ml copy toner powder until dissolved.
Add 10 ml kerosene to the mixture and mix well.
Transfer the mixture to a spray bottle for easy application.
Clean and dry the test section surface before each application of the oil mixture.
Use the spray bottle filled with the oil mixture to spray a thin, even layer of fluid over the section of interest.
Initiate the image or video acquisition on the camera before powering on the wind tunnel.
Set the suction wind tunnel to the desired velocity once the camera is recording.
Stop the camera recording and power down the wind tunnel when the oil mixture reaches a steady state or after the desired time has elapsed.
Prepare the test section floor surface by drilling holes for mounting stainless steel tubulations.
Drill holes on a grid that spans 8.89 cm in the spanwise direction and 22.86 cm downstream with 1.27 cm spanwise grid spacing and 2.54 cm downstream grid spacing.
Mount the stainless steel tubulations flush with the test section floor surrounding the anchor position of the prolate hemispheroid.
Attach pieces of short flexible tubing from the mounted stainless steel tubulations to the scanning pressure transducer measurement ports.
Connect the scanning pressure transducer to a computer.
Configure the acquisition parameters using the scanning pressure transducer software.
Set the acquisition software to acquire data at 500 Hz for the desired duration of data acquisition.
Set the suction wind tunnel to the desired velocity.
Begin pressure measurement acquisition.
